nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are some recycled synthetic fibres?
nodes.answer: Polyester, nylon, and polypropylene can be recycled through mechanical or chemical processes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_001
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What statistical analyses were performed to determine the predictors of sustainable plastics behaviour?
nodes.answer: Four linear regression analyses were conducted to assess the extent to which socio-demographic, psychological, and economic variables predict sustainable plastics behaviour.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Which two self-reported plastic sustainable consumer behaviour (SCB) statements were the most commonly reported by the respondents?
nodes.answer: The two most common SCBs reported were reusing plastic products and disposing of plastics in a recycling bin.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_003
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why do Waste Laggards tend to participate more in reusing plastics rather than in purchasing or disposal actions?
nodes.answer: Waste Laggards are more likely to reuse plastic items because it provides direct benefits like cost or time savings. Purchasing and disposal behaviours are perceived to be more time-consuming and costly, making them less appealing to this group.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_004
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some examples of sustainable plastics behaviours that consumers engage in during the usage phase?
nodes.answer: During the usage phase, consumers engage in sustainable plastics behaviours such as reusing plastic containers and refilling water bottles.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the main finding of Abeyance et al.'s systematic review on behaviour change against the use of non-biodegradable plastic bags?
nodes.answer: The main finding of Abeyance et al.'s systematic review is the effectiveness of interventions in promoting behaviour change against the use of non-biodegradable plastic bags.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Reusable and recyclable plastics_qna_006
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How did Bell et al. (2016) aim to increase recycling participation in Wisconsin households?
nodes.answer: Bell et al. (2016) aimed to increase recycling participation in Wisconsin households through single-stream programs.
